newsitem.title: CHINA: Powerful typhoon zeroes in on Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Powerful typhoon zeroes in on Hong Kong.

text.p: A powerful typhoon headed straight for Hong Kong on Saturday, severely disrupting air, land and sea traffic and forcing the Chinese territory's 6.4 million residents to batten down the hatches.
People had earlier rushed to supermarkets after businesses closed early, braving torrential rain to stock up with food and other essentials ahead of what threatened to be a turbulent night.
Traffic snarled as people headed home to barricade doors and windows against Typhoon Victor, which threatens to be the most destructive to hit this region of southern China since 1983.

By early evening, though, Hong Kong streets were deserted as the Hong Kong Observatory issued a rare number nine typhoon warning signal, just one grade below the "10" signal heralding a super tropical cyclone.
A number nine signal, forecasting winds with speeds above 118 km an hour (73 mph), was also hoisted in nearby Portuguese-ruled Macau, where air and sea traffic was already badly disrupted.
The Hong Kong Observatory said Victor was expected to make landfall very close to Hong Kong this evening if the typhoon followed its present track.
It did not rule out the possibility that Victor would pass directly over the territory. A spokesman said there was a chance the number 10 signal could be hoisted.
At 7 p.m. (1100 GMT) the storm was centred about 30 km (19 miles) south of Hong Kong and forecast to move north at about 22 km per hour (14 mph), the observatory said.
More than 100 flights due to leave or arrive in Hong Kong have already been diverted, delayed or cancelled, a spokesman for Hong Kong's Civil Aviation Department told Reuters.
Ferry services to outlaying islands and to Macau were cancelled. Victoria Harbour, one of the world's busiest, was emptied as ships docked in typhoon shelters.

Bus and railway services were also suspended, while the underground rail system provided limited service. The Tsing Ma bridge, one of the world's largest suspension bridges which links Lantau Island to the Kowloon peninsula, was closed because of strong wind.
The Hong Kong government said Victor had so far caused no serious damage. Only one minor landslip and four minor flooding incidents had been reported. No one was hurt.
Across the Pearl River estuary, Macau's small international airport was closed and bus services in the Portuguese-ruled outpost were also shut down.
Hong Kong's TVB television news said minor flooding had occurred in some areas of Macau.
The Hong Kong government urged people to take precautions, board up windows and doors. Schools were closed and government employees sent home.
Victor is the most powerful typhoon to approach Hong Kong since Typhoon Ellen in 1983,, which caused serious damage here.
